title: Check Operational State Transitions: Running ↔ Bag Out/Close Out, Then Shutdown (State Model)
summary: Verify that the live system follows the operational state model: after bag out/close out completes, the system automatically returns to the running state; chutes are closed during the close/bag-out phase; and shutdown is the last state chosen from the Viva HMI (not an automatic end-of-bag-out behavior).
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm that the system’s operational state transitions match the expected cycle after bag out/close out, and that shutdown is only entered when selected from the HMI.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a remediation guide for specific state-transition failures; the source does not provide corrective actions beyond escalation.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Observe the live system state indicators on the Viva HMI and confirm whether transitions match the expected running ↔ bag out/close out ↔ running behavior, and whether shutdown is entered only via HMI selection.
access_or_tools_needed: Viva HMI (used to put the system into shutdown)
Any live system view used to observe current state (exact UI elements not named in the source)

system_preconditions: System is in an operational cycle where running, bagging out/close out, and shutdown states can be observed.

visual_references.description: Training frame containing the state-model discussion: running/bagging out/close out, chutes closed, automatic return to running after bag out, and shutdown chosen from the HMI.

steps.title: Identify the current system state (running vs bagging out vs close out)
steps.purpose: Establish the starting point so you can verify the expected next transition in the state model.
steps.instruction: On the live system view (Viva HMI or other live state indicator available to you), determine whether the system is currently in one of the main states described: “running,” “bagging out,” or “close out.”
steps.expected_result: You can classify the current system state as running, bagging out, or close out based on the live state indicator you are viewing.
steps.healthy_condition: The live state indicator clearly corresponds to one of the model’s main states (running / bagging out / close out).
steps.failure_condition: The live state cannot be classified into the model’s main states, or the state indicator appears inconsistent with the expected cycle context.

actions.label: Check current state indicator
actions.exact_action: Observe the live system state indicator and classify it as running, bagging out, or close out.

source_evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: “for the most part, you're either running, bagging out, or we called it close out originally.”

steps.title: Verify the close out / bag out transition back to running
steps.purpose: Confirm the expected automatic behavior after close out/bag out completes.
steps.instruction: If the system is in bagging out or close out, observe the transition after completion and confirm that it returns to the running state automatically.
steps.expected_result: After bag out/close out completes, the system returns to the running state automatically.
steps.healthy_condition: The live state indicator changes from bagging out/close out back to running without requiring shutdown selection.
steps.failure_condition: The system does not return to running after bag out/close out completes.

actions.label: Observe post-bag-out transition
actions.exact_action: Wait for bag out/close out completion and confirm the state indicator returns to running.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the system does not return to running after bag out/close out as described.

source_evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: “after a close out it goes back into a running state.”
“the system OK automatically once it's done with bag out, it will go to a running state.”

steps.title: Confirm chute condition concept during close/bag-out and running-to-close/bag-out behavior
steps.purpose: Validate that the cycle’s chute condition aligns with the model’s close/bag-out phase behavior.
steps.instruction: During the close out/bag out phase, confirm the chute condition concept described: “the chutes are closed.” Also confirm that the system can go from running to close or bag out and then returns to running afterward.
steps.expected_result: Chutes are closed during close/bag-out, and the system transitions running → close/bag out → running afterward.
steps.healthy_condition: Live indicators you can observe show the system entering close/bag-out with chutes closed, then returning to running afterward.
steps.failure_condition: Chutes are not closed during the close/bag-out phase, or the running → close/bag-out → running sequence does not occur as described.

actions.label: Check chute condition concept
actions.exact_action: Observe the live chute condition/state during close/bag-out and confirm it matches “chutes are closed,” then observe the subsequent return to running.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the observed behavior does not match the described running ↔ close/bag-out ↔ running behavior.

source_evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: “Now the chutes are closed. So technically you could go from running to close or bag out and it goes back into a running state afterwards.”

steps.title: Confirm shutdown is selected from the HMI and is the last state
steps.purpose: Ensure shutdown entry matches the model: shutdown is chosen from the HMI and is the last state.
steps.instruction: If shutdown is observed, verify it aligns with the rule that shutdown is something you choose from the HMI (Viva HMI) and is the last state shutdown.
steps.expected_result: Shutdown is entered only after an HMI selection (Viva HMI), and it appears as the last state in the cycle.
steps.healthy_condition: The live state indicator shows shutdown only when you (or the operator) selected shutdown from the Viva HMI, and it occurs after the running/bag-out/close-out cycle.
steps.failure_condition: Shutdown appears without the described HMI selection behavior.

actions.label: Check shutdown entry behavior
actions.exact_action: Observe the live state indicator showing shutdown and confirm it was entered via the Viva HMI shutdown selection (not automatically at end of bag out).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if shutdown appears without the described HMI selection.

source_evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: “Shutdown is the end of that is something you choose from the HMI choose from it.”
“UPS using a Viva HMI, we'll put in a shutdown.”

success_criteria: Observed state transitions match the model: running → bag out/close out → running automatically after bag out/close out completes.
Chutes are closed during the close/bag-out phase conceptually as described.
Shutdown is only entered as a chosen last state from the Viva HMI (not automatically at end of bag out).
healthy_conditions: System returns to running after bag out/close out completes.
Chutes are closed during close/bag-out phase and the system returns to running afterward.
Shutdown is entered only via Viva HMI selection and appears as the last state.
failure_conditions: System does not return to running after bag out/close out.
Running → close/bag-out → running sequence does not occur as described.
Shutdown appears without the described HMI selection behavior.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if state transitions do not follow the described running/bag out/close out/shutdown behavior. The source does not provide remediation steps.
